messages:
incident-bot: Pager ALERT - INC-4215 inference-runtime-high-latency P1 triggered (service: hosted-api)
Liam: handing off — been on since 22:00 PT. short summary: big spike in KV cache misses causing long tail token latencies and a few 502s for streaming requests. scaled pool + rolling restart bought time but 95p latency still ~2.1s.
Maya: thanks. quick Q — are any customer-facing fallbacks active (model downgrade / region routing)?
Liam: yes — canary routing to older quantized variant enabled for 10% of traffic ~22:14. fallback worked for most traffic but a few high-throughput customers still seeing errors. no DB changes.
Priyanka: I’m picking up secondary. I can watch metrics and take the scale/route actions if needed.
Liam: confirmed — Maya you take primary. Priyanka secondary. Sara, can you own comms (status page + customer slack) while I finish some cleanup? I’ll be reachable for 30m. :wave:
Sara: on it. I’ll draft a short status now and ping legal for any SOC flags.
Maya: I’ll drive the incident. immediate checklist I’ll follow (and leaving notes in the runbook):
```
# quick mitigation steps (INF-RT-003)
1) scale inference pool: rctl scale --env prod --pool inference-hosted --replicas 6
2) toggle canary routing: rctl route set --service hosted-api --policy canary --weight 10
3) restart frontend workers gradual: k roll restart deploy/frontend -n prod --batch 10%
4) watch KV cache hit rate + GPU utilization (grafana link in thread)
```
Liam: also FYI we saw increased RPC queueing from redis cluster node 7 — I bumped reconnect settings and it settled. still want to check redis tail logs.
Priyanka: I’ll tail redis and watch for reconnect errors. linking runbook metrics: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/inf/kv-cache?orgId=1
Tom: small coverage note — APAC on-call window has a 4h gap between rotations tonight (02:00-06:00 UTC). not critical right now but flagging in case escalation required.
Maya: good catch. I’ll try to get a follow-up shift swap if we expect prolonged recovery. for immediate next actions: I’ll own incident lead, Sara owns external comms, Priyanka owns metrics/automations, Liam stays on-call for 30m.
Sara: draft status: "Investigating elevated latencies for hosted inference. We’ve routed a portion of traffic to a lower-latency variant and scaled capacity. Some customers may experience transient errors; we are monitoring and will update." posting in #status-pages now. :pencil:
Liam: leaving one todo — collect stack traces from a failing request and upload to the incident doc. pointing to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-4215/traces/
Priyanka: grabbing traces now. tailing redis logs.
devops-bot: Autoscaler executed: added 2 replicas to inference-hosted (trigger: manual request by Liam)
Maya: thanks team. I’ll keep the thread updated with milestones (latency 95p back under 1.0s, errors <0.1%). if we hit that we’ll start de-escalation.
Sara: posted initial status, linked contact for affected customers. will post updates every 15m or on major milestone.
Liam: back to odd-hours. good handoff. :thumbsup:
Maya: accepted — taking over. logging this handoff in the runbook and Jira INC-4215.
incident-bot: Note: escalation policy unchanged. Next on-call: Priyanka (secondary) -> Pager if severity increases.
Maya: end of handoff notes: driving=true; comms_owner=Sara; secondary=Priyanka; outgoing=Liam (reachable 30m).
